title: Limit: The Freedom of Setting Boundaries
coreMove: Set visible limits early enough that other people can plan around them and the essential is no longer endlessly available.
sourcePressure: The chapter shows that boundaries protect time from being hijacked and reduce the need to renegotiate every request from scratch.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: A weak run would write about personal boundaries as generic self-care without connecting them to protected contribution.

hook: generic limit: the freedom of setting boundaries topic opener
tryThisNow: set a timer for ninety seconds...
make a list of priorities without a trade-off
generic say no to one thing today

exampleSpecs.domain: public library setting visible study-room booking limits during exam week
exampleSpecs.audience: library manager tired of daily renegotiation
exampleSpecs.stakes: unclear limits let a few groups capture shared space
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: She posts a two-hour booking rule and waitlist path beside the room keys before the first complaint arrives.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Study-room keys hang below a new booking rule.

exampleSpecs.domain: community clinic protecting walk-in vaccine hours from sales reps
exampleSpecs.audience: clinic lead whose time is hijacked politely
exampleSpecs.stakes: patients lose access when no visible limit exists
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: She points to the posted vendor window and keeps the vaccine line moving instead of negotiating in the hall.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A posted vendor window sits beside vaccine tickets.

exampleSpecs.domain: youth soccer league limiting parent sideline coaching
exampleSpecs.audience: league director protecting players and coaches
exampleSpecs.stakes: without boundary, every match becomes another negotiation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Before, coaches argue every weekend; after, a sideline line and one appeal table change the match rhythm.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A sideline line is painted beside an appeal table.

exampleSpecs.domain: shared ceramics studio reserving kiln access for finished glazes only
exampleSpecs.audience: studio manager protecting scarce kiln time
exampleSpecs.stakes: unbounded exceptions spoil firings for everyone
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: She tapes the glaze-test rule to the kiln log and refuses a wet exception before loading.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A kiln log hangs beside a glaze-test tile.

exampleSpecs.domain: court clerk setting document-review cutoff before daily filing deadline
exampleSpecs.stakes: boundary protects fair access instead of personal comfort
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: He reviews the missed filing stack and adds a visible cutoff stamp to the intake tray.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A cutoff stamp sits on the intake tray.

exampleSpecs.domain: neighborhood tool library defining late-return consequences
exampleSpecs.stakes: friendliness without limits makes tools unavailable to others
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: She places the overdue saw beside the loan board and writes the late-return rule before texting a friend.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: An overdue saw lies under a loan board.
